title: D'BEAST: Logged Bad Experiences as Explanation for Autonomous Driving Agents
abstract: arXiv:2611.20019v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Reinforcement learning agents learn from mistakes, yet their decisions can be difficult to trace back to those experiences. We investigate whether a tabular agent's decisions can be explained by its bad experiences, defined as the training transitions associated with safety or task events. A fixed training log is replayed from the same initial Q-table under three conditions. FULL retains all updates, SKIP omits bad-experience updates, and NEUTRALIZE retains those updates without their event penalties. We illustrate the method on six classic Markov decision processes and evaluate it in closed-loop driving in CARLA. On the full driving task, FULL reached the goal from 33 of 40 test starts, whereas SKIP and NEUTRALIZE reached it from none, indicating that the bad experiences carry decision-relevant information. translated_title: D'BEAST：将记录的糟糕经验作为自动驾驶智能体决策的解释依据
translated_abstract: 强化学习智能体从错误中学习，但它们的决策往往难以追溯到这些经验。我们研究表格型智能体的决策能否由其“糟糕经验”来解释，糟糕经验被定义为与安全或任务事件相关联的训练转移。我们从一个相同的初始Q表出发，在三种条件下重放固定的训练日志：FULL保留所有更新，SKIP省略糟糕经验的更新，NEUTRALIZE保留这些更新但不施加其事件惩罚。我们在六个经典马尔可夫决策过程上展示该方法，并在CARLA中进行闭环驾驶评估。在完整驾驶任务中，FULL从40个测试起点中的33个成功到达目标，而SKIP和NEUTRALIZE无一成功，这表明糟糕经验承载着与决策相关的信息。在局部层面，针对SKIP或NEUTRALIZE失败前不久的47个决策，移除或中和一小部分糟糕经验……
tldr: 该论文提出D'BEAST方法，通过在移除或中和与安全/任务事件相关的“糟糕经验”更新的条件下重放训练日志，证明这些糟糕经验承载了决策关键信息，从而为自动驾驶智能体的行为提供解释。
en_tdlr: D'BEAST explains autonomous driving agents' decisions by replaying training logs and showing that removing or neutralizing logged "bad experiences" tied to safety or task events dramatically changes behavior, demonstrating that these experiences carry decision-relevant information.
